Petitioners file this petition for quashing of the FIR No.245/2017 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Punjabi Bagh, Delhi against them and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. The marriage between the petitioner No.1 and complainant/ respondent No.2 was solemnized on 03.05.2013 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies at Delhi.

However, due to matrimonial discord,
the couple could not live together and on the complaint of respondent No.2 aforesaid FIR was registered against the petitioners.
The charge sheet was filed by the police.
The petitioner No.1 obtained the divorce on the ground of cruelty from learned Competent Court and even appeal filed by respondent No.2 was dismissed.
During the pendency of proceedings, the couple has settled the matter per settlement agreement dated 22.07.2022 before Counselling Cell, Family Courts, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi.

entities.text: Counselling Cell, Family Courts, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Pursuant to settlement, the petitioner No.1 has agreed to pay Rs.7.50 Lacs to respondent No.2 towards all her claims of alimony, maintenance - past, present and future,
stridhan, and dowry articles etc.
3.

Out of said sum, the petitioner No.1 has already paid Rs.4.50 Lacs to respondent No.2 and for the balance amount, the petitioner No.1 has handed over draft No.660347 dated 27.02.2023 drawn on Bank of Baroda for Rs.3.00 Lacs in favour of respondent No.2, which has been accepted by her.

1 4.
The complainant/respondent No.2 has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, states the matter has been settled with the petitioners and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
The learned APP for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.
The affidavits of parties are on record.

5. Considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the FIR as complainant has settled all the disputes and has received the settled amount from the petitioners.
In view of the above, there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioners as it would never entail in conviction of petitioners.
6. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, FIR No.245/2017 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Punajbi Bagh, Delhi and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
